title: Operations Charter: Authorization & Supplier Guidance
author: Maya Chen
body:
Purpose
This charter defines company-wide operational rules for who may grant access, how changes to production and sensitive systems are managed, how data must be classified and handled, and standard procedures for supplier lifecycle, procurement, expenses and travel approvals. It unifies approvals, thresholds, and templates so cross-functional teams can operate consistently and with auditability.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, full-time contractors, and third-party vendors with system or data access.
- Covers: identity & permissions, change management for infra/services, data classification & handling, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding/offboarding, and travel expense rules.
- Does NOT replace team-specific runbooks; instead provides company guardrails and escalation paths.

Principles
- Least privilege: grant the minimum access required and review every 90 days for long-lived access.
- Separation of duties: approval chains must include an independent approver where financial or security risk exists.
- Auditability: every elevation, procurement, or vendor onboarding event must be traceable in the ticketing and contract systems.
- Risk-based controls: higher-risk assets (production, customer data, keys) require stronger controls and multi-party approval.

Key Roles and Responsibilities
- Requester: person initiating access/change/procurement/travel. Responsible for justification and required artifacts.
- Approver: manager or designated owner who verifies business need and scope.
- Security Reviewer: reviews high-risk access and changes involving customer data or secrets. (Owner: Security)
- Procurement Owner: procurement or finance representative who approves spend commitments and vendor terms. (Owner: Finance)
- Supplier Manager: assigned owner for vendor relationship (owner_team: customer-success or product as applicable).
- IT/Platform Executor: engineering team member who performs the approved change or config.

Authorization Matrix (summary)
- Low-risk (read-only documentation, public dashboards): manager approval. Access TTL: up to 30 days by default.
- Medium-risk (non-production infra, internal dashboards, dev keys): manager + security notifier. Access TTL: 30–90 days.
- High-risk (production systems, customer data, KMS/HSM, production DBs): manager + security reviewer + infra owner. Access TTL: < 30 days, just-in-time where possible.
- Emergency/Break-glass: follow Incident Response procedures; emergency access must be recorded and reviewed within 3 business days.

Change Management Workflow (production-facing changes)
1) Create a change ticket in the company tracking system with: scope, rollback plan, impact window, testers, and SLO impact assessment.
2) Automated pre-check: CI and unit/integration test pass; canary plan & metrics defined.
3) Approvals: team lead + change co-owner + security (if secrets or customer data). For changes > $100k spend impact, procurement notified.
4) Schedule & Execution: change executed by an approved executor within scheduled maintenance window.
5) Post-change verification: success criteria validated; rollback executed if failure.
6) Postmortem: required for failed changes or those with > 5% SLO degradation.

Change Thresholds and SLO Impacts
- Minor: config changes that do not touch customer data or require infra reconfiguration. Approver: team lead. No scheduled window required.
- Standard: code or infra change affecting non-production systems or limited production surface. Approvers: team lead + infra owner. Scheduled maintenance window recommended.
- Major: schema changes, migrations, or rollouts affecting production traffic or customer data. Approvers: team lead + infra owner + security + product. Canary rollout mandatory.

Data Classification & Handling
- Public: safe for external distribution (marketing collateral, anonymized metrics). No special controls.
- Internal: Redwood internal business information (internal roadmaps, team docs). Store on internal systems, shared with company accounts.
- Confidential: contains proprietary business or customer information; access limited, encryption at rest & in transit required.
- Restricted: regulated data or PII/PHI requiring contractual controls and restricted hosting (e.g., VPC/private deployment). Requires security and legal approval for processing.

Handling Rules
- All Confidential/Restricted datasets must be registered in the Data Inventory and have a documented retention schedule.
- Backups for Confidential/Restricted data must be encrypted with KMS-managed keys; key access audited quarterly.
- Data exports require an export request ticket including purpose, recipient, and retention; exports of Restricted data require legal sign-off.

Procurement & Expenses (summary of process)
- Low-value purchases (<= $2,000): team lead approval and submit expense via expense system. Preferred payment: corporate card or reimbursement.
- Mid-value purchases ($2,000–$50,000): procurement owner + finance approval. Must include vendor evaluation (at least 2 quotes if available), security questionnaire completion for cloud services, and contract review.
- High-value commitments (>$50,000 or multi-year): procurement + legal + finance + VP-level approval. Board-level notification for multi-year > $500k.
- Capital vs. Operational: Procurement owner tags purchases and coordinates budgeting entries.

Vendor Lifecycle: Onboarding to Offboarding Checklist
Onboarding (minimum):
- Business justification and owner assignment.
- Security questionnaire completion (third-party security assessment).
- Contract template (legal) signed; include data processing addenda if applicable.
- Payment method and invoicing details registered.
- Access scoped and time-limited; initial access granted only after contract execution.
- Supplier Manager assignment and SLAs recorded.

Quarterly Review & Risk Reassessment:
- Suppliers with access to Confidential/Restricted data undergo a quarterly risk review.
- Renewal decisions based on performance, security posture, and cost.

Offboarding:
1) Terminate access (IAM, SSO, VPN, service accounts) within 24 hours of contract termination.
2) Revoke API keys, rotate shared credentials, and ensure data return/destruction clauses are executed.
3) Archive contracts and invoices in the vendor repository.

Travel & Expense Highlights
- Pre-approval: All business travel must be pre-approved by the Requester's manager with an estimated budget in the travel system.
- Daily per-diem and hotel caps: Domestic US: $250 per day total (meals + incidentals); International by region (see travel system rates). Any exceptions require director-level pre-approval.
- Flights: economy class for trips < 6 hours; premium economy or business requires VP approval for > 6 hours.
- Receipts: submit itemized receipts for all expenses > $25. Missing receipts must be explained; repeated missing receipts may delay reimbursement.

Auditability and Recordkeeping
- All approvals must be preserved as part of the ticket or contract record for at least 7 years for financial transactions and 5 years for access/change artifacts (or longer if required by contract/regulation).
- Every change or access approval must include the approver name, timestamp, and justification.

Templates and Examples (copy-paste ready)
- Access request example (ticket body):
  Purpose: Short business need
  Asset: e.g., "prod-db-replica"
  Duration: start/end or TTL
  Justification: specific tasks and risk mitigation
  Rollback plan (if change): steps to revert

- Procure request metadata example (YAML):
  vendor: "Acme GPU Solutions"
  sku: "r-infer-32x"
  estimated_cost: "$27,400"
  business_owner: "ML Platform"
  security_review: "completed"
  contract_reference: "CTR-2026-0123"

- Vendor security checklist snippet (to be attached to onboarding ticket):
  - SOC2 or equivalent: yes/no
  - Data processing addendum required: yes/no
  - Encryption at rest: yes/no
  - Pen-test history last 12 months: yes/no

Exception Handling and Appeals
- For exceptions to thresholds (spend or access TTL), submit an Exception Request with: business impact, alternative options considered, compensating controls, and proposed expiration.
- Approvals for exceptions follow an elevated chain: manager -> procurement/finance -> security/legal (for data-related exceptions) -> VP for record retention.

Enforcement and Metrics
- Quarterly compliance reports generated by the Governance team: number of open exceptions, reoccurring vendors with findings, average procurement cycle time, percentage of privileged access reviewed within SLA.
- Targets: 100% of high-risk access requests reviewed within 5 business days; vendor security questionnaires completed before production access 95% of the time.

Change Log (major updates)
- 2024-09-15: Initial charter published.
- 2025-02-10: Added travel caps and clarified emergency access review SLA.

Useful Links and Next Steps
- Submit new access/change/procurement requests via the company ticketing portal.
- Register sensitive datasets in the Data Inventory before any development work.
- Contact Security (security@redwood.com) for quick clarifications on classification or emergency approvals.

Appendix: Quick checklist for Requesters
- Have you documented the minimum access required?
- Have you included rollback and validation steps?
- Is there a Supplier Manager assigned for vendor requests?
- Is there a legal contract or PO issued for spend > $2,000?

Glossary
- Supplier Manager: the internal owner responsible for vendor relationship and SLA enforcement.
- TTL: time-to-live for temporary access.
- KMS: Key Management Service.

Questions or feedback about this charter: contact the document owner (owner_team: finance-legal).
